newsitem.title: BELGIUM: U.N. says Zaire force should have arrest powers.
newsitem.headline: U.N. says Zaire force should have arrest powers.

text.p: The United Nations refugee chief said on Thursday that a "neutral force" sent by the international community should be empowered to arrest and disarm militias and other groups operating in lawless eastern Zaire.
"I would like to see them empowered to do that, that should be one of their functions if such a force goes in," U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees Sadaka Ogata told Reuters.

The UNHCR has been widely criticised for feeding and sheltering the leaders of the Hutu-inspired genocide of up to one million Tutsis in Rwanda in 1994. Several of them fled, along with hundreds of thousands of Hutu refugees, into eastern Zaire after the defeat of the then government.
Ogata said it had not been possible to arrest and detain many of the known perpetrators in the camps without causing massive unrest that weak local authorities were unable to deal with.

Ogata and leaders of other international aid agencies are attending a meeting of EU development ministers to try and find a solution to the deteriorating situation in the Great Lakes area of central Africa where an estimated 1.2 million refugees have been created by a new bout of fighting.
